datasheet_id_and_revision: SLOS436A, March 2004, revised July 2004 (appended package option addendum dated 11-Nov-2025 and package materials pages dated 14-Oct-2026)
datasheet_status: Production data (p1 footer: PRODUCTION DATA information is current as of publication date)
citation_convention: pN = 1-based PDF page index; for p1-p22 the printed page number equals N; p23-p37 are unnumbered addendum, package and notice pages. EC = Electrical Characteristics table. Fig N = datasheet figure number.
value_types: TYP = typical at 25 C. MIN/MAX = limit; the EC tables give a test level per row: A = 100% tested at 25 C, over-temperature limits by characterization and simulation; B = limits set by characterization and simulation; C = typical value only for information. CURVE = read from a typical-characteristic plot (uncertainty stated).
input_type: bipolar (BiCom3 silicon-germanium process, p1; the datasheet does not say 'bipolar' explicitly; consistent with 7 uA typical input bias current, p4)
compensation: unity-gain stable voltage feedback (3 GHz small-signal bandwidth at G = +1, p4 EC, p9 Fig 1 and Fig 3)

min_stable_gain.what_datasheet_says: Characterized at G = +1 (SSBW 3 GHz, VO = 100 mVpp); Fig 1 shows ~+4 dB peaking at G = +1 with VO = 100 mVpp. p15: 'Care must be taken to ensure that parasitic elements do not erode the phase margin'; capacitance at the output and inverting input and resistance/inductance in the feedback path cause problems; for G = +1 use a wide trace directly between output and inverting input. No guidance on capacitive (TIA) feedback or noise-gain shaping.
min_stable_gain.open_loop_phase_margin_estimate: ~45 deg at the ~0.9 GHz unity-gain crossover (CURVE, Fig 26, +/-5 deg)

tia_content_note: No transimpedance example, figure, table or equation anywhere in the datasheet.
application_guidance: p15: remove ground plane under the part; short direct feedback traces; G = +1: wide trace from output to inverting input; G = +2: RF = 249 Ohm keeps peaking ~2 dB with good layout, 499 Ohm gives ~5 dB peaking; lower RF reduces peaking but degrades distortion with heavy loads; 0.1-uF ceramic bypass close to the part. HD2: single-point ground between supply bypass caps on split supplies; single reference point for input termination and gain resistors; follow EVM layout. p16-p22: EVM schematics/BOM/layouts (split +/-2.5 V and single 5 V), differential ADC driver for ADS5500 (SFDR ~84 dB to 40 MHz, Fig 56).
abs_max_and_input_protection: Supply +6.0 V; input voltage +/-VS; differential input +/-2 V; output current 150 mA; TJ 150 C max (125 C for long-term reliability); ESD HBM 1600 V, CDM 1000 V, MM 100 V (p3). No input-protection circuit described.
other_notes: Single-supply part (2.7-5.5 V): output swing 1.1-3.9 V at 5 V/100 Ohm, i.e. ~2.8 Vpp max; Fig 30 overdrive test clips at ~1.5/3.5 V (narrower than the EC swing).
Fig 13 is titled '2ND HARMONIC DISTORTION vs OUTPUT VOLTAGE' but its y-axis label reads '3rd Harmonic Distortion - dBc' (p10).
p6 EC (3 V) lists two slew-rate rows with identical condition 'G = +2, VO = 1-V Step' (750 and 675 V/us).
Ordering table p2 gives DGK rails of 100; addendum p23 gives tube of 80.
Zout EC row (0.016 Ohm at 100 kHz) carries test level A although it is a typical value.
Other qualified version: THS4304-SP (space) listed in addendum p24.
